name: stale-cached-report-renderer
description: Fix a report renderer whose on-disk cache serves stale output after changes to templates, reference data, or settings — including files that are created or deleted between runs
scenario: ReportForge is a command-line tool that generates formatted HTML reports from CSV data. It caches rendered reports on disk to speed up repeated runs. Users report that after updating source files — product names in the catalog, exchange rates, formatting settings — the reports still show the old information. Deleting the /app/cache directory by hand fixes it temporarily, but the problem returns as soon as the cache is repopulated. The --fresh flag also works as a per-run workaround. One user noted that adding a new overrides configuration file had no effect until they cleared the cache manually.
environment_setup: The Dockerfile installs PyYAML and copies the ReportForge Python package to /app/reportgen/, along with templates (/app/templates/), CSV data (/app/data/), reference data (/app/refdata/products.json and rates.json), and config (/app/config/formatting.yml). The optional overrides file /app/config/overrides.yml does NOT exist by default. The cache lives in /app/cache/. Three interacting bugs exist: (1) loader.py uses lazy dependency registration — load functions call register_dep() as a side effect during rendering, but the cache lookup happens before rendering, so lazily-registered deps (products.json, rates.json, overrides.yml) are invisible to cache validation; (2) cache.py's store() silently skips dependency files that don't exist on disk instead of recording them as missing, so creating a previously absent dependency file after caching doesn't invalidate the entry; (3) cache.py's lookup() compares only the intersection of current dependency hashes and manifest entries, so files present in only one dict (newly created or newly deleted) are silently ignored. Each behavior looks locally reasonable; the defect emerges from their composition.
instruction_summary: Fix ReportForge so that after any change to any file that affects report output, re-running the same report command always produces output reflecting those changes. The cache should still work (identical inputs produce a cache hit, avoiding re-renders). Command: python3 -m reportgen <report_type> --data <csv_path> --from <start> --to <end>. Output is printed to stdout as HTML.
solution_outline: In __main__.py or loader.py, eagerly register all possible dependency paths (products.json, rates.json, overrides.yml) before the cache lookup step, so get_dependency_paths() returns the complete list at both lookup and store time
In cache.py store(), record non-existent dependency files with a None sentinel value instead of silently skipping them

In cache.py lookup(), compare the full union of current dependency hashes and manifest entries — not just the intersection — so that newly-created files (in current but not manifest) and deleted files (in manifest but not current) both cause invalidation
In cache.py lookup(), handle None sentinels: if manifest has None and file now exists → invalidate; if manifest has a real hash and file is now missing → invalidate
test_plan: test_product_name_change: Run report, change a product name in products.json, run again, verify new name in output
test_exchange_rate_change: Run report, change rates.json (set EU→USD to 999.0), run again, verify output differs and reflects new rate
test_formatting_change: Change currency_symbol in formatting.yml to €, run report, verify € appears in output
test_template_change: Change template heading, run report, verify new heading in output
test_cache_hit_no_change: Run report twice without changes, verify identical output (cache still works)

test_overrides_created_after_cache: Delete overrides.yml if present, run report (caches without it), create overrides.yml with currency_symbol: £, run report, verify £ appears — catches partial fix that doesn't handle non-existent deps in store() or intersection-only lookup

test_overrides_modification: Write overrides.yml with currency_symbol: £, run report, verify £ appears; then change to ¥, run again, verify ¥ appears — catches partial fix that eagerly registers deps but doesn't handle missing-file sentinels

test_file_deleted_after_cache: Run report with all files present, delete overrides.yml, run report, verify output no longer shows overrides — catches partial fix that doesn't handle deletion (intersection-only lookup ignores manifest entries with no current hash)
test_different_data_file: Create a new CSV with different transactions, run report with it, verify output reflects new data
anti_cheat: Expected outputs are not stored anywhere in the image. Tests independently modify input files and verify the report output changes accordingly. A solution that hard-codes output or deletes the cache entirely would fail the cache-efficiency test. Tests use different modifications (different symbols, rates, names) so hard-coding specific values cannot pass.
failure_modes: An agent may eagerly register products.json and rates.json (fixing the most visible lazy-registration gap) but miss overrides.yml because it is conditionally loaded, passing most tests but failing the overrides tests. Alternatively, eagerly registering all deps but not fixing store()'s missing-file handling passes when all files already exist (the agent's re-test) but fails when overrides.yml is created from scratch after caching. A third trap: fixing store() sentinels but leaving the intersection-only comparison in lookup() means deleted files are still invisible to validation.

faults.where: reportgen/loader.py and reportgen/__main__.py — lazy dependency registration via register_dep() side effects
faults.what: Dependency paths for products.json, rates.json, and overrides.yml are registered lazily when their respective load functions are called during rendering. The cache lookup calls get_dependency_paths() before rendering, so these lazily-registered deps are absent from the validation set. Only the eagerly-registered static deps (template, formatting.yml, data file) are validated.
faults.symptom: Changing exchange rates, product names, or creating/modifying overrides has no effect on cached reports
faults.how_discovered: Trace the rendering pipeline: cache lookup → render → cache store. Notice that register_dep() calls happen inside load_products(), load_rates(), and load_overrides(), all of which are called during rendering — after the cache has already been checked. Compare the dep list at lookup time vs store time.
faults.wrong_fix: Eagerly register products.json and rates.json before cache lookup (because they always exist and are always needed), but leave overrides.yml as lazily/conditionally registered since it's optional and may not exist
faults.counterexample: Create overrides.yml with currency_symbol: £, run report → output still shows $ because overrides.yml was never registered at lookup time and isn't in the validation set
faults.why_normal_case_passes: Changing rates.json now correctly invalidates the cache; modifying an already-existing overrides.yml also works if it was registered during a prior render. The agent's re-test (modify rates.json, modify existing overrides.yml) succeeds.
faults.caught_by_test: test_overrides_created_after_cache creates overrides.yml from scratch and checks for £ in output; test_overrides_modification writes then modifies overrides.yml

faults.what: Silently skips dependency files that don't exist at store time (the `if os.path.exists(dep_path)` guard before hashing), instead of recording them as missing. A file created later is invisible to the manifest, so the cache entry is served stale.
faults.symptom: If overrides.yml doesn't exist when a report is first cached, creating it later doesn't update the report
faults.how_discovered: Reason about the lifecycle: what happens if a tracked dependency is absent at cache-write time but appears later? Read store() and notice the exists guard drops the entry entirely rather than marking it missing.
faults.wrong_fix: Eagerly register all deps including overrides.yml, but don't fix store()'s handling of non-existent files — the file appears in the dep list but store() still skips it when it's absent
faults.counterexample: Delete overrides.yml, run report (cache entry written; store skips overrides.yml so manifest has no entry for it), create overrides.yml with currency_symbol: £, run report → stale output still shows $
faults.why_normal_case_passes: If overrides.yml already exists when first cached, store() hashes it normally; modifying it changes the hash and correctly invalidates the cache. The agent's re-test (edit existing overrides.yml after eagerly registering it) passes.
faults.caught_by_test: test_overrides_created_after_cache deletes overrides.yml, caches a report, creates the file, re-runs, and checks for £

faults.what: The lookup compares current dependency hashes against the manifest by iterating over the intersection of their keys: `for dep_path in set(current_hashes) & set(manifest)`. Files present in the manifest but absent from current_hashes (deleted since caching) and files present in current_hashes but absent from the manifest (created since caching) are both silently ignored, so neither deletion nor creation invalidates the cache.
faults.symptom: Deleting a reference file or creating a new one after a report is cached does not cause the cache to invalidate
faults.how_discovered: Trace the lookup logic: after computing current_hashes (which also skips non-existent files via an exists guard), the comparison uses set intersection. Reason about what happens to manifest entries whose files have been deleted, or current files that weren't in the manifest.
faults.wrong_fix: Fix Faults 1 and 2 (eager registration and store sentinels) but leave the intersection-based comparison in lookup. Since sentinels ensure every dep is in the manifest, newly-created files now have a sentinel entry and ARE in the intersection — so creation works. But deleted files are not in current_hashes (exists guard) and thus fall out of the intersection, so deletion after caching still serves stale output.
faults.counterexample: Cache a report with overrides.yml present (manifest has its hash). Delete overrides.yml. Run report → output still shows the old overrides because the manifest entry for overrides.yml is not in the intersection (file absent → not in current_hashes → not compared)
faults.why_normal_case_passes: The agent's re-test involves modifying existing files (which stay in both dicts) or creating new files (which, after store-sentinel fix, have a manifest entry and are in the intersection). Deletion is not part of the agent's natural re-test because the visible symptom only mentions updates and additions.
faults.caught_by_test: test_file_deleted_after_cache caches with all files present, deletes overrides.yml, re-runs, and verifies the output no longer reflects the deleted overrides

hidden_edge_cases: Creating a dependency file from nothing after a cache entry already exists (overrides.yml created post-cache)
Deleting a tracked dependency file after a cache entry was written with it present
An overrides.yml containing only YAML comments (parsed as None by safe_load) vs one that doesn't exist — both result in no overrides applied, but are different states for the cache manifest
Running with --fresh produces correct output but doesn't fix the cache invalidation for subsequent non-fresh runs
Rapid create-delete-create cycle: delete overrides, cache, create overrides, cache again, delete overrides — each transition must invalidate
why_not_textbook: This is not a standard cache-invalidation pattern like HTTP ETags, CDN purge, version-busting query strings, or the well-known 'cache key omits a parameter' bug. The specific interaction — lazy side-effect-based dependency registration that is temporally misaligned with cache validation, combined with a store that silently drops missing files and a lookup that compares only key intersections — is bespoke to this codebase. No well-known bug (Pillow ANTIALIAS, nginx trailing slash, etc.) covers it.
static_read: Reading loader.py shows get_dependency_paths() returns _registered_deps and various load functions call register_dep(). Reading cache.py shows the exists guard in store() and the intersection comparison in lookup(). However, each piece looks like reasonable defensive code — lazy registration is a common pattern, the exists guard prevents errors on optional files, and the intersection comparison avoids KeyError on mismatched dicts. The bug only manifests when you trace the full execution sequence: deps are registered after the cache already validated, missing files are erased from the manifest, and the intersection silently drops both new and deleted entries.
crux: A cache validation system must account for the full lifecycle of every file that can affect output: it must know about all such files at validation time (not just at store time), it must record their absence as a distinct state (not erase them from the manifest), and it must compare the complete set of tracked files (not just the intersection of what exists now vs what existed before). Each of these three requirements is violated by code that looks locally correct.
sequence_invariant: After any change to any file that affects report output, re-running the same report command always produces output reflecting those changes. This includes creating a previously absent file or deleting a previously present one.
nameable_fix: eagerly register all dependencies, record missing files as sentinels, and validate the full dependency set
self_check_blind_spot: The agent modifies an existing file (e.g., rates.json or an already-present overrides.yml) and re-runs the report, which works correctly after eagerly registering deps. The failing sequences — creating a file that didn't exist when the cache entry was written, or deleting a file that did exist — are not part of the agent's natural re-test because the visible symptom only mentions updates to existing files.
reference_in_environment: None. No code in the environment correctly handles the missing-file sentinel case, the lazy-registration timing, or the full-set comparison. The README lists all input files and describes the caching behavior but does not state the validation completeness rule.
interaction: 1. loader.py's load functions register dependencies lazily (as side effects during rendering), under the assumption that anything calling get_dependency_paths() does so after rendering. 2. __main__.py calls the cache lookup before rendering, under the assumption that get_dependency_paths() already knows all deps. 3. cache.py's store() skips non-existent files under the assumption that a missing file cannot change. 4. cache.py's lookup() compares only the intersection of current and stored dep sets under the assumption that both sets have the same keys. Each component's local assumption is reasonable; the defect emerges when they compose: the cache validates an incomplete set of deps, erases missing files from the manifest, and ignores entries that don't appear on both sides of the comparison.
